QF.id: AIFM CII AIFs in India and Suitability_8

question.text: Himalaya Venture Debt Fund (Category II) is structuring a INR 50 crore venture debt facility to a Series-B-funded SaaS start-up. The term sheet debates the size of the 'equity kicker' typically attached via warrants to the debt. Per Chapter 3, what is the CUSTOMARY upper limit for the equity kicker in Indian venture-debt deals, expressed as a percentage of the loan amount?

answer.text: Up to 2% of the loan amount
Up to 25% of the loan amount
Up to 10% of the loan amount
Up to 49% of the loan amount

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 3, Section 3.2.2 (Debt Fund / Private Debt Fund): 'Usually, venture debt comes with an equity kicker upto 10% of the loan amount.' The section also notes that venture debt currently constitutes only 8-9% of overall VC financing in India, leaving headroom for scalability. The Trap: 2% is too low relative to the risk of unsecured lending to asset-light start-ups. 25% would make the instrument look more like mezzanine/quasi-equity than venture debt. 49% would effectively be a co-equity deal and conflict with the Cat II 25% single-investee concentration limit. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same 10% figure. XV (Research Analyst) touches venture-debt valuation. Cat III leverage mechanics (different from kicker math) are XIX-E territory and are not tested here. Manager's Pro-Tip: Negotiate the warrant strike price at the last priced round (not at the next round), and cap the warrant coverage at 10% cashless-exercise-equivalent — founders will push for a 20% discount to the next round, but that effectively doubles your dilution when the next round is up.
